title: acs review verdict
description: The verdict /acs:review-code writes for one iteration, and the one document that crosses the review loop to /acs:code. NOTE: the invariant that makes this a verdict rather than a self-report -- `passed` must equal "no blocking finding still standing" -- is NOT expressible here and is enforced by acs_lib.verdict.validate_verdict, which is what the hooks actually run. This schema pins the shape; that function pins the meaning. Refuted findings never appear here: they stay in iter-<n>/adjudication.json as an audit trail.

run_id.description: The run this verdict belongs to.

reviewed_sha.description: The commit the review judged. /acs:code copies it into result.json as `since_sha` and diffs from it; the next review prioritises the hunks changed since.

lens.description: Set only on a single lens's own report; the verdict the coordinator writes carries null.

passed.description: DERIVED, never asserted: true exactly when no `blocking` finding is still standing.

id.description: `F-<iteration>-<n>`, stable across iterations: a re-raised finding keeps its id so the next review can close it and /acs:code can answer it.

status.description: `confirmed` blocks and must be answered by id. `advisory` is carried, never gating -- a `needs-context` adjudication lands here rather than being dropped. `resolved` closes a previous iteration's finding, so the trail shows closure.

kind.description: `gate` is stage 3's channel: a build, lint, suite or coverage failure is a finding with the failing command as its evidence, which is why the gate needs no separate report to the loop.

lens.description: Which lens raised it. Lens B fans out across the diff, so several findings may carry B; the letter names the lens, not the instance.

claim.description: One sentence: what is wrong and why it matters.

evidence.description: What the review established -- file:line ranges, commands and their output, an absent test named. So /acs:code does not re-derive it.

resolved_when.description: The refutation criterion the adjudicator could not satisfy, restated as what a fix must make true. Required on a confirmed finding: it is what /acs:code works to.

traces_to.description: `TC-n` / `AC-n` when a lens can name them; empty otherwise.

tests.description: The final gate's run of the full unit suite (§3.6 stage 3), as numbers rather than prose. It is the only place the full suite runs in the pipeline: /acs:code iterates against the tests its change touches. states.tests is derived from here, so the recorded result is the review's independent finding rather than the implementer's self-report. Optional: a docs-only subject has no coverage to record, and a run can end before any review writes a verdict.

skipped.description: Why no run was taken on this iteration. The gate runs only when stage 2 leaves nothing blocking -- the changeset is going back to /acs:code, so a run against this tree answers a question nobody will ask. A deferral is never a pass: a zero-findings verdict requires a green run on the iteration being passed.

coverage.description: Coverage read off the SAME run recorded in `tests`, not a second one: on most repos the test command reports coverage because it is the command the coverage gate runs. `percent` is the measured figure; the target it is judged against comes from settings.test_coverage_percent, never from here.

skipped.description: Deferred with the run it is read from; same rule.
